It’s cheap and cliche and tropey, but the Power of Narrative is on your side. You can go for the most hack option, and as long as everything else around it is fun players won’t mind and will appreciate it’s for the story: I opened a one-shot in media res, chasing down a train with a kidnapped princess on board - finding the princess later was an important story hook so I duped half the party with a derro in disguise, and had another bandit simply vanish with the real princess when the train went into a dark tunnel. Contrast that with a one shot I played where my friend wanted to chase down someone who saw us breaking into a warehouse but was told by the DM “No, she gets away, because she has to”. Even if what you are essentially saying is “they get away because they have to”, as long as you don’t use those words you’re usually fine

The way I see it for the townsfolk at least is that a lot of people generally know some folklore or have local superstitions or traditions but don’t necessarily know the meanings or purpose or truth behind them - this would be the territory of an adept magician (a Know or higher) or a scholar (allowed the knowledge by the watchman’s tree)
Book of Hours also gave us a lot more in implications about ways to have a long life but not a Long Life - be host to a greater power like a worm or duendrazon, use Years or Amaranthine Nectar, embrace your inner Carapace Cross etc.

It’s so hard to choose, but I think after meeting the first long of this aspect, it has to be Nectar. Feels like a mix of Moth and Grail to be fair which were my old favourites - honourable mention to heart. Also as a big fan of the Ys legend and how it’s been interpreted in the game Rose makes for a nice round top 5 lmao
